MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "Master of Reality feels like a natural choice because Black Sabbath's heavy riffs connect with the metal side of my recent listening.",
    "That choice recognizes that heaviness matters to me, even when the album comes from an earlier era than most of my recent picks."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "Every Kingdom, The Best of Branigan, and the Sting concert lean toward acoustic folk or polished pop rather than the heavier guitars I want now.",
    "The blues-oriented live set and orchestral pop of Together We're Heavy do not offer the same appeal as my recent hard rock and metal choices.",
    "GREEN ROOM, Compositions, and Heartbroken and Homicidal do not give me enough recognizable musical context to make me choose them; an ambiguous or dark title alone is not a match."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "Sharing a broad connection to rock seems to count for too much, even when the actual sound is much softer or more blues-oriented.",
    "Dark or heavy-sounding wording does not tell me whether I will enjoy the music."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My repeated choices of albums such as Colony, Reroute to Remain, and Soundtrack to Your Escape suggest a sustained interest in heavier music, rather than a passing interest in rock generally.",
    "My latest choices, Ten Thousand Fists and 10.000 Days, reinforce my current appetite for heavy, forceful music.",
    "Age alone is not decisive: I would choose older Black Sabbath for its heavy sound, while a general 1965 rock compilation feels less connected to what I want."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "You picked up on my interest in rock, but most choices missed the particular heaviness that makes it appealing to me right now."
}
